item.title: Video: ‘It’s a boy!’ — Peller, Jarvis unveil baby’s gender
item.description: Nigerian TikTok personalities Peller and Jarvis have announced that they are expecting a baby boy. The couple shared the news in separate social media posts, expressing excitement and gratitude as they prepare to welcome their child. Peller, announcing the baby’s gender, wrote: “Today, our hearts are fuller than ever. It’s a BOY!Our little blessing, we can’t wait to hold you in our arms. ” The couple also shared an emotional message, describing the pregnancy as the fulfilment of their prayers and dreams. Today, our hearts are filled with a kind of happiness words can never fully explain. God has blessed us with a precious gift, and we can’t wait to hold you in our arms, kiss your little face and show you how much you are loved. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Amadou Elizabeth Aminata (@realjadrolita) “My child, you may not know it yet, but you are already the reason behind so many smiles, tears of joy and endless prayers. We love you already. “Thank You, Lord, for this precious gift. ” The announcement was accompanied by a video in which the couple revealed the baby’s gender, attracting reactions from fans and followers. Peller and Jarvis are popular Nigerian internet personalities known for their TikTok content and online presence. item.title: Fela, Queen Latifah, Phil Collins Join Rock Hall Of Fame
item.description: The rhapsodic hip-hop transformers Wu-Tang Clan and punk rocker Billy Idol were among the music luminaries inducted Saturday into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame at a star-studded concert gala. The versatile Phil Collins, post-punk and electronic dance music renegades Joy Division/New Order, and the velvet-voiced late Luther Vandross also joined the rock pantheon at the ceremony held in Los Angeles’s Peacock Theater. But several of the 2026 class of artists — Oasis, Sade and Iron Maiden — skipped the night celebrating their honor, one of the music industry’s most prestigious. But the show went on. Staten Island’s own Wu-Tang Clan — the ragtag group of New Yorkers who paired raw production with streetwise rhymes and martial arts influences — brought the ruckus, performing their own hits including “C.R.E.A.M” and “Wu‐Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit.” “We went from being banned on the radio to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame,” said member Method Man onstage to resounding cheers. To the haters, he said, “you can kiss my inducted ass.” It proved a banner night for women in hip-hop, with honorees including Queen Latifah as well as MC Lyte, who is widely recognized as the “First Lady of Hip Hop.” The storied performers tore up the stage with a medley of their hits, before Megan Thee Stallion and Remy Ma joined them to underscore the legacy of women in rap. Travis Barker, the drummer from Blink-182, inducted Collins, drawing tears from the British artist who attended the ceremony alongside his children, including Lily of “Emily in Paris” fame. US rapper/actress Queen Latifah attends the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on November 14, 2026. (Photo by VALERIE MACON / AFP) Collins — whose entry into the hall is his second, the first was as part of the band Genesis — walked to the stage with two canes, taking the mic and saying, “I’m really not as bad as it looks.” “You haven’t heard the last of me, I can promise you that.” Cynthia Erivo belted out Collins’s smash “In The Air Tonight,” with Barker playing the instantly recognizable drum fill. “My life has just been one thing after the other, one dream after the other,” Collins said to journalists backstage. item.title: 2027: SERAP Gives INEC Seven Days To Prosecute Electoral Violence Suspects
item.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has given the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) seven days to prosecute persons arrested over reported incidents of electoral and political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections or face legal action. SERAP made the demand in a letter dated November 14, 2026, and addressed to INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, urging the commission to obtain relevant case files and investigation materials from the Nigeria Police Force and prosecute suspects where sufficient evidence exists. The organisation also asked INEC to direct its legal officers or appointed legal practitioners to review the files and promptly initiate prosecutions under the Electoral Act 2026. The demand follows several reported incidents of political violence across the country since campaigns for the 2027 elections began on 19 August, including the latest attack on members and supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in Oregun, Lagos, on 12 November. In the letter signed by its Deputy Director, Kolawole Oluwadare, SERAP urged Amupitan to press the police to conclude investigations into other reported attacks, arrest suspected perpetrators and their sponsors, and forward relevant evidence to INEC. It also called on the commission to exercise its powers under Section 83 of the Electoral Act 2026 to demand explanations from political parties suspected of involvement in or encouraging prohibited conduct and impose prescribed fines on those that fail to comply with lawful directives. SERAP expressed concern over reports of attacks on political convoys, party secretariats, rallies and meetings, as well as intimidation of candidates and supporters. Cited incidents included the reported obstruction of the convoy of NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi in Benue State on 8 September; attacks on political meetings in Enugu State on 12 September; and the attack on the convoy of ADC senatorial candidate Herberta Okonofua in Edo State on 6 October. Others included attacks on supporters of Accord governorship candidate Oriyomi Hamzat in Ibadan on 14 October, which reportedly resulted in one death, and the attack on the convoy of NDC candidate Rollins Offia-Nwali in Ebonyi State on 22 October, which allegedly left one person dead and three injured. The organisation also cited the reported attack on African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore and his team in Ado-Ekiti on 30 October, the attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar on 4 November, and an NDC procession in Asaba on 7 November, which reportedly left one person dead and five injured. It added that journalist Samuel Adebanjo was assaulted and his equipment seized while covering the November 12 incident in Lagos. item.title: Former APC spokesman warns of crisis if Tinubu is imposed in 2027
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Former Deputy National Publicity Secretary of the ruling All Progressives Congress APC, Timi Frank, has warned that any attempt to force President Bola Tinubu back into office in 2027 could plunge the country into crisis. Frank, who is the Ambassador to East Africa and the Middle East of the United Liberation Movement for West Papua (ULMWP), said Nigerians would not accept an outcome that contradicts their votes. “Nigerians will not accept a situation in which someone is declared the winner when the people know they did not vote for him. They should not push the country into a crisis by attempting to impose him on the people,” Frank warned. He urged the president to abandon his re-election ambition and guarantee a transparent electoral process. “Whoever wins should be allowed to emerge as the choice of the people,” he said. Frank also expressed concern over alleged attempts by some political actors to manipulate the electoral process. He described the public protest against Tinubu after prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in Area 1, Garki, Abuja, last Friday as evidence of growing dissatisfaction with the administration. Tinubu reportedly faced boos from some Hausa protesters who chanted “Ba ma yi” (we don’t want you) after the prayers. In a viral video, some protesters were seen removing and destroying his campaign posters and billboards in parts of Area 1. Frank condemned the protesters for choosing a religious occasion to vent their displeasure and commended the President’s security detail for ensuring his safety and de-escalating the situation. He nevertheless urged the President to recognise the significance of the public reaction. “The rejection was total and unmistakable. No Nigerian president has been embarrassed like this publicly. The way Nigerians rejected him speaks volumes but should he decide to go ahead and he loses, he should be prepared to accept defeat just like former President Goodluck Jonathan did,” he said. The former APC spokesman said he was worried by what he called a growing gap between the assurances given to the President by political associates and the mood of the people. “I have seen the confidence with which some people are assuring President Tinubu that he will win the Federal Capital Territory FCT and that he is firmly in control. But the reported embarrassment he suffered during a prayer session in Abuja tells a different story. “What happened in the FCT last Friday showed that political assurances and promises are not necessarily a reflection of the reality on the ground. item.title: NGE demands release of detained investigative journalist, Ojukwu
item.description: The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has condemned the arrest, detention and prosecution of Daniel Ojukwu, an investigative journalist with the Foundation for Investigative Journalism (FIJ), demanding his immediate release on bail. The Guild also called for a review of the criminal charges against Ojukwu and FIJ founder, Fisayo Soyombo, warning that the prosecution could undermine press freedom and discourage investigative journalism in Nigeria. Ojukwu is currently being held at the Kuje Correctional Centre, Abuja, after being arraigned on a 12-count charge bordering on alleged cyberstalking and criminal defamation. In a statement dated November 15 and signed by its President, Eze Anaba, and General Secretary, Onuoha Ukeh, the NGE said it was alarmed that a journalist was facing criminal prosecution over reports raising questions about the expenditure of public funds by the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Sustainable Development Goals. The Guild said Ojukwu’s investigation reportedly exposed an alleged payment of more than ₦147 million, approximately $109,000, to an Abuja-based restaurant for the construction of classrooms and a skills acquisition centre at a primary school in Lagos. According to the NGE, the investigation raised questions about the existence of the projects, as well as the capacity and track record of the company involved in the contract. It described the issues raised by the investigation as legitimate matters of public accountability that deserved transparent answers rather than the prosecution of the journalist who brought them to public attention. The Guild expressed particular concern that Ojukwu had been remanded in prison despite pleading not guilty to the charges, while his bail application, initially scheduled for November 12, was adjourned until December 1. It said the resort to arrest, detention and criminal prosecution over journalistic work raised concerns about the commitment of authorities to press freedom, freedom of expression and Nigerians’ constitutional right to information. The NGE recalled its opposition to the alleged use of cybersecurity laws by the police and other security agencies to harass, intimidate and bully journalists. “Investigative journalism is not a crime. Asking questions about public expenditure is not cyberstalking. Demanding accountability from public officials is not defamation,” the Guild said. It maintained that public office holders must be open to scrutiny over their management of public resources, adding that journalists should not face threats of arrest, prosecution or imprisonment for reporting alleged irregularities. While acknowledging the right of individuals to seek legal redress over publications they consider injurious to their reputation, the Guild warned against using such rights to intimidate journalists or suppress legitimate investigations. item.title: AFCON 2027: 6 countries who need a win to keep qualification hopes alive
item.description: Six countries are facing an uphill battle to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) after losing all three of their opening matches in the qualifying campaign. Lesotho, South Sudan, Somalia, Sierra Leone, Central African Republic and Liberia are yet to record a point after three rounds of matches, leaving them bottom of their respective groups . With three matchdays remaining, the six countries will need to turn their fortunes around quickly to stand a realistic chance of securing a place at the tournament. Lesotho occupy the bottom position in Group A after suffering three consecutive defeats. Their latest setback came against Gabon, who secured a 2-0 victory on Friday, November 13. The result left Lesotho without a point, while group leaders Morocco maintained their perfect record with a 5-1 victory over Niger to move to nine points. South Sudan are experiencing a similarly difficult campaign in Group B, having lost their third consecutive match following a 2-0 defeat to Angola on Saturday, November 14. The South Sudanese side are bottom of the group with zero points, eight behind joint leaders Egypt and Angola, who have both collected seven points. In Group C, Somalia are also struggling after losing 2-0 to Ghana on Thursday, November 12. The defeat marked their third straight loss, leaving them at the bottom without a point. Ivory Coast lead the group with nine points after beating Gambia 2-1, while Gambia remain second with six points. Sierra Leone are another country under pressure after losing all three of their opening fixtures in Group E. Their latest defeat came against DR Congo, who secured a 3-1 victory on Thursday, November 12, to maintain their position at the top of the group with nine points. Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea occupy second and third positions with four points each, while Sierra Leone remain bottom without a point. Central African Republic have also endured a disappointing start to their qualifying campaign in Group F. They suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat to Benin on Thursday, November 12, leaving them with three losses from three matches. Benin and Burkina Faso are joint leaders of the group with seven points each, while Mauritania occupy third position with three points. Liberia complete the list of six winless countries after losing 4-2 to Cape Verde on Friday, November 13. The defeat left Liberia bottom of Group K without a point, while Mali lead the group with nine points following their 3-2 victory over Rwanda. Rwanda are second with six points, while Cape Verde have three. Although the six countries have made difficult starts, none has been mathematically eliminated from the qualification race, with three rounds of matches still to be played. The fourth round of qualifiers begins on November 16, giving the struggling teams another opportunity to secure their first points and revive their campaigns. item.title: Iran attacks US military base in Bahrain
item.description: Explosions rocked Bahrain early Sunday as Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it had launched a drone attack on a United States military base in the Gulf nation. The attack came amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East, with Bahrain experiencing fresh Iranian strikes after a lull in attacks. Sirens sounded across the country, while authorities issued several emergency alerts on social media, urging residents to seek shelter. The warnings were the first since September. Bahrain, which hosts a major US naval base, has now been targeted twice in three days. The country’s military said it intercepted several Iranian attacks, preventing them from reaching their intended targets, while the Foreign Ministry confirmed that air defence systems had shot down Iranian drones. Explosions were heard around 4:00 a.m. (0100 GMT), according to an AFP journalist, while residents reported another series of blasts around 6:30 a.m. In a post on X, Bahrain’s Interior Ministry urged residents to remain calm, move to the nearest safe location and follow updates through official channels. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said their Aerospace Force carried out the attack on a US radar system at a military installation in Bahrain. “The US air defence radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain was targeted by six drones belonging to the IRGC Aerospace Force,” the Guards said in a statement carried by Iranian state television and posted on Telegram. “The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and any aggression by the American enemy will be met with an even harsher and more forceful response,” the statement added. Iran has restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a major global oil transit route, during more than eight months of war, while targeting infrastructure including airports, seaports, energy facilities and US assets across the region. Bahrain condemns attacks Bahrain is among the Gulf countries that have faced thousands of Iranian drone and missile strikes since the conflict began on February 28. In a statement, the country’s Foreign Ministry rejected the use of its territory as a battleground in the conflict and held Iran responsible for the attacks and their consequences. Bahrain “rejects turning its territory into an arena for settling scores and holds Iran fully responsible for these attacks and their consequences,” the ministry said. On Friday, the Revolutionary Guards had announced that they targeted a US early-warning radar system in Bahrain, marking the first reported strike against a Gulf country since early September. The US military’s Central Command (CENTCOM), which oversees American military operations in the region, said it shot down two Iranian drones targeting the Gulf island, adding that the attack caused no casualties or damage. item.title: Nigerian property owner in US named among worst landlords after building collapse kills eight
item.description: A Nigerian property owner, Olufemi Falade whose building collapsed onto an adjacent construction site in Brooklyn, New York, killing eight people, reportedly owes more than $450,000 in unpaid taxes, water bills and government fines. The property owner has also been listed six times on the New York City public advocate’s annual “Worst Landlords Watchlist” over allegations of poor property management. According to the New York Post, an examination of city records showed that Falade accumulated most of the outstanding debts through the three-storey building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue, which collapsed on Wednesday. The records indicated that he owes $170,000 in fines issued by the Department of Buildings in 2019 over improperly displayed signs, alongside $114,945 in unpaid water bills and $113,526 in property taxes dating back to 2021. Falade also reportedly owes the Internal Revenue Service $49,269 in unpaid personal federal income taxes, according to a 2010 lien, as well as another $4,316 in personal income taxes to New York State. The building, which had 98 outstanding violations with the city’s Department of Housing Preservation and Development before the collapse, reportedly had a history of maintenance and safety problems. The violations included a leaking roof, defective doors, bedbug infestations and exposed electrical wiring. Records showed that complaints over the leaking roof dated back to 1976, with further violations issued as recently as this year. Falade purchased the 96-year-old property in 1999 through an entity known as Femi Realty Corp. In November 2024, he transferred ownership to another company he controls, Isolag Realty Corp, signing the deed as both seller and buyer without any money changing hands. The report also revealed that Falade was sentenced to 12 days in jail in 2006 and fined $50,000 for civil contempt after failing to address more than 1,800 violations across 12 Brooklyn buildings he owned at the time. Meanwhile, questions have emerged over the approval of excavation plans at an adjacent construction site believed to have contributed to the collapse. The New York City Department of Buildings reportedly approved the excavation plans in March for a proposed three-storey, 25,000-square-foot mixed-use development at 2625 Bedford Avenue. However, the approved plans allegedly failed to provide adequate structural reinforcement alongside the building that subsequently collapsed. Real estate attorney Massimo D’Angelo, of Blank Rome, called for improved coordination between city agencies responsible for property safety and enforcement. item.title: Bishop Onah mourns four UNN students, commends Ortuanya’s leadership
item.description: By Alumona Ukwueze NSUKKA —The Catholic Bishop of Nsukka Diocese, Most Rev. Prof. Godfrey Igwebuike Onah, has joined the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), community in mourning the death of four students following a tragic incident at an off-campus house party. Bishop Onah, who paid a condolence visit to the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Simon Ortuanya, on Friday, expressed sympathy and solidarity with the university community over the incident. He commended Ortuanya for his prompt response, particularly his efforts to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths and his assurance that a thorough investigation would be conducted to determine the actual cause of the tragedy. The cleric expressed admiration for the Vice-Chancellor’s handling of the incident, noting that similar leadership qualities should be demonstrated at other levels of governance in the country. He also praised the Vice-Chancellor for identifying with the families of the deceased students and ensuring that the surviving students received necessary medical attention. While consoling the university community, Bishop Onah urged students to heed the Vice-Chancellor’s advice, abide by the institution’s rules and regulations and make judicious use of the opportunity to acquire university education. He further advised them to conduct themselves responsibly and remain focused on their academic pursuits, which he described as their primary reason for being in the institution. The Vice-Chancellor had on Thursday declared a three-day mourning period in honour of the deceased students. Ortuanya also visited the surviving students in various hospitals where they are receiving treatment, assuring them of the university management’s commitment to supporting their medical care and recovery. item.title: Insecurity: Forgive me for not visiting communities, Tinubu begs Plateau residents
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has appealed to residents of Plateau State to forgive him for not visiting communities affected by recurring attacks, particularly Angwan Rukuba in Jos North Local Government Area, following the March 29 killings. Tinubu made the appeal on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Jos, where he acknowledged the devastation caused by years of violence in the state. The president explained that his previous visit to Plateau was restricted to the airport, but insisted that he had seen the extent of the destruction and received reports on the situation from Governor Caleb Mutfwang. “When I last visited, the other time, I was limited to the airport; forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland, but I saw the devastation,” Tinubu said. “I got the report from the governor; I saw the horror in the faces of our people. “At the end of the day, we are fighting together; it is now that we can rebuild, and I assure those displaced that we will rebuild your communities, and we will bring you back to your community.” Tinubu, who acknowledged that attacks in Plateau since 2001 had claimed lives, destroyed homes and displaced communities, assured affected residents that his administration would support efforts to rebuild their communities and facilitate the return of displaced persons. He also urged residents to embrace peaceful coexistence, saying differences in language and other identities should not divide them. “Living in different rooms and speaking different languages does not make us enemies of one another. We have to live together, we have to farm together, we have to build this Plateau and this country together,” he said. The president also expressed condolences to families who lost loved ones, survivors of the attacks and residents whose homes were destroyed or who remained unable to return to their communities. “To every bereaved family, every home destroyed, every survivor, and everyone unable to return home, I offer my heartfelt condolences for your loss,” he said. On March 29, several residents of Angwan Rukuba were killed when unidentified gunmen opened fire on people at a popular bar in the community. The attackers were suspected to be cultists. Following the incident, Tinubu, during a visit to Jos in April, ordered the deployment of 5,000 artificial intelligence-enabled surveillance cameras to strengthen security in Plateau State. During the visit, he sympathised with the victims’ families, saying no amount of compensation could make up for their losses. He also met with stakeholders and some victims at the Plateau airport. However, his failure to visit the affected communities during that trip attracted criticism from Nigerians, some of whom questioned his decision to restrict his visit to the airport. item.title: Police arrest suspected terrorism financiers, bandits’ motorcycle suppliers
item.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The Police Force Intelligence Response Team (IRT) has arrested suspected terrorism financiers, alleged motorcycle suppliers to bandits, armed robbery suspects and suspected kidnappers in separate intelligence-led operations across Kaduna and Plateau states. The operations also led to the recovery of five firearms, comprising two pistols and three locally fabricated pistols, as well as a motorcycle and a stolen Toyota Corolla. The Force Intelligence Department disclosed this during a briefing on the operational achievements of the IRT in Abuja, saying the operations formed part of sustained efforts to dismantle criminal networks involved in kidnapping, banditry, armed robbery and terrorism-related activities. Speaking at the briefing, IRT Commander, Deputy Commissioner of Police Adamu Muazu, said two suspects, identified as Nura Umar, 20, from Kidandan, and Alhaji Rabiu Aliyu, 58, from Zaria, Kaduna State, were arrested over alleged involvement in kidnapping and banditry-related activities. According to him, the suspects were arrested on August 29, 2026, following intelligence linking them to the supply of motorcycles to bandits operating in Kaduna and Katsina states. The police said the suspects allegedly confessed to supplying several motorcycles to bandit groups in the two states. One Honda CV-125 motorcycle without a registration number was recovered during the operation. The police described the arrests as significant to efforts to dismantle the financial and logistical networks sustaining kidnapping and banditry, adding that investigations were ongoing to identify other accomplices and trace the financial channels supporting the alleged activities. In another operation, the IRT arrested three suspected members of a criminal gang allegedly involved in one-chance operations, car snatching and armed robbery in Kaduna and its environs. The suspects were identified as Abdullahi Abubakar, Yusuf Mohammed and Bala Ibrahim. Abubakar was arrested on October 12, 2026, at about 8:30pm, following intelligence linking him to a gang allegedly targeting residents, particularly commercial tricycle and motorcycle operators. The police alleged that members of the gang strangled their victims before dispossessing them of their valuables. According to the police, Abubakar, who had previously served a 13-year jail term for a similar offence, identified a suspected gang leader, Boniface, said to be currently in Kaduna Prison. The police alleged that Boniface directed Abubakar to a hideout where the gang’s operational firearms were kept. Following the execution of a reproduction warrant, operatives recovered two pistols from the location. Further investigations reportedly led to the arrest of Mohammed and Ibrahim, who were identified as alleged receivers of stolen vehicles, motorcycles and tricycles. item.title: Navy uncovers 56,800 litres of stolen crude in Rivers
item.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has deactivated two illegal refining sites and uncovered approximately 56,800 litres of suspected stolen crude oil in Ogbogolo community, Ahoada West Local Government Area of Rivers State. The operation, conducted on November 13, 2026, was carried out by personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Soroh, a unit under Operation Delta Sentinel, following credible intelligence on illegal refining activities in the Orashi Forest. Director of Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this in a statement, saying the operation uncovered two illegal refining sites containing one refining oven, 22 dugout pits and four sacks of suspected stolen crude oil. According to him, the first site contained approximately 1,800 litres of crude oil, while the second held an estimated 55,000 litres. He said the recovered products and associated items were subsequently handled in accordance with established anti-crude oil theft procedures. Folorunsho said the operation underscored the Nigerian Navy’s commitment to dismantling illegal refining infrastructure and disrupting networks involved in crude oil theft. He added that the Navy would continue to deploy intelligence-driven operations to deny oil thieves access to the nation’s petroleum resources and protect critical oil and gas infrastructure. The Navy, he said, remained committed to sustaining operational pressure on crude oil thieves and illegal refiners in support of national crude oil production, economic security and the protection of Nigeria’s maritime interests. item.title: [VIDEO] Taraba Records 72 Road Crash Deaths In 10 Months – FRSC
item.description: No fewer than 72 people died in 115 road traffic crashes recorded in Taraba State between January and October 2026, the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has said. The FRSC Sector Commander in Taraba, Anna Attah, disclosed this during a press briefing in Jalingo to mark the 2026 World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims. She said 374 people sustained injuries in the crashes, identifying excessive speeding and dangerous driving as major causes. Attah also said Nigeria recorded 7,156 road crashes, 3,445 deaths and 22,292 injuries between January and September 2026. item.title: 2027: Umo Eno backs Wike’s Rainbow Coalition for Tinubu
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has declared support for the Rainbow Coalition led by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. Eno said he was willing to join any political coalition whose central objective was to secure Tinubu’s return to office in the 2027 presidential election. Speaking during a media chat on Saturday, the governor said he had thrown his weight behind the Rainbow Coalition, describing it as a platform for supporting the president. “That Rainbow Coalition is simply saying that we support President Tinubu as the president,” Eno said. He added: “If I will join and be a member of any coalition — whether it is Rainbow, call it any name. Any coalition that the central point is supporting the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu; I am for it.” The governor also said the relationship between the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Akwa Ibom State remained cordial, noting that both parties had reached an understanding on their political direction ahead of the 2027 elections. According to him, the arrangement involves supporting Tinubu, Senate President Godswill Akpabio and himself in the forthcoming elections. “I will work with all of them, and I think we are good on the ground in Akwa Ibom when it comes to the PDP-APC relationship,” he said. “We have agreed on the fact that we are supporting the president, we are supporting the Senate President, we are supporting the governor, and we have our clear understanding about those things.” BACK STORY The Rainbow Coalition, a cross-party political movement associated with Wike, has generated differing reactions within the APC, particularly over its implications for the party’s structures and candidates ahead of the 2027 general election. In September, APC leaders in the South-East backed the Progressive Governors’ Forum (PGF) in insisting that all party candidates should receive support in the 2027 elections. The leaders also rejected what they described as the “Rainbow (chameleon) Coalition”, warning that the party would resist any attempt to undermine its structures in the region. Their position followed the PGF’s declaration that it would not support any alliance or political arrangement capable of undermining Tinubu’s re-election bid or the electoral prospects of APC candidates. The governors were reportedly referring to the Rainbow Coalition, which Wike, a PDP member, has been promoting as a cross-party platform. In January, Wike said the coalition represented a departure from conventional party politics towards a collective political movement focused on advancing the interests of the state. item.title: 2027: ADC will defeat Tinubu in 13 Northern states – Amaechi
item.description: Rotimi Amaechi, the vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has expressed confidence that the party will defeat President Bola Tinubu in all 13 states of the North-East and North-West in the 2027 general election. Amaechi also predicted that the ADC would make significant inroads into the South-South and North-Central regions, specifically naming Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states as territories the party expects to win. He spoke on Saturday at the ADC presidential campaign rally in Bauchi, where he warned that the party would not accept what he alleged was a repeat of the electoral events of the 2023 general election. “Because these people will do what they did in 2023. This time, we shall not agree. Do you understand? We will not do what?” he said. The former Minister of Transportation said the ADC had a stronger political presence across the North-East and North-West, which comprise 13 states. “We are the only party that comes with 13 states. The whole of North-East, the whole of North-West, that is 13, right? Let the president tell us how many states he comes with. He comes with only five in the South-West,” he said. Amaechi further predicted that the APC would lose another state in the South-West to the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). “That’s if he will. And the sixth state in the South-West will vote APM, whether he likes it or not,” he added. He said the ADC would challenge the APC in the South-South and North-Central, expressing confidence that the party would win Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states. “We will fight with him in South-South. We will fight with him in North-Central. And be sure, be rest assured, Niger, Kogi, Nasarawa will be in ours easily,” he said. On the South-East, Amaechi dismissed the prospect of Tinubu making significant electoral gains in the region, insisting that the ADC would emerge victorious. “He will not go to South-East at all. item.title: Tinubu has performed credibly in North, deserves second term – Bichi
item.description: The Chairman, House Committee on Appropriations, Rep. Abubakar Bichi, says President Bola Tinubu has performed credibly in Northern Nigeria. Bichi, who stated this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria in Dutse, Jigawa, insisted that the region had benefited significantly from Tinubu administration’s policies and development projects. He described the growing support for Tinubu’s reelection in the North as impressive. He said the turnout of people from the North at the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential campaign rallies was a clear indication of their satisfaction with the achievements of Tinubu. “Contrary to claims in some quarters that Tinubu does not care about the North. “The president has demonstrated commitment to the development of the region through major infrastructure and other intervention projects. “The turnout of people from the north is impressive, and it is a clear testimony that the people are happy with what Tinubu has done so far. “President Bola Tinubu has performed credibly in the North, and there is no state that has been left out,” Bichi said. He cited Jigawa as an example, explaining that the president had approved about N80 billion for the Greater Dutse Water Project to address one of the state’s major developmental challenges. He also highlighted ongoing and completed road projects in the state, particularly the Kano-Hadejia road, which he said, covered approximately 200 kilometres. According to him, the section from Kano to Danja has been completed, while work on the Danja-Hadejia stretch has reached about 80 per cent completion. Bichi further said that several irrigation projects had also been completed in Jigawa. He noted that such interventions demonstrated the federal government’s commitment to improving infrastructure and agricultural development in the region. “As Chairman of the House Committee on Appropriations, I know what President Tinubu has done in many parts of the North, and it is fantastic,” he said. Bichi dismissed suggestions that the president was indifferent to the welfare of Northern Nigerians. The lawmaker maintained that Tinubu administration had recorded significant achievements across the North-West and other parts of the region. “Some people are saying what they want to say, that President Tinubu doesn’t care about the north and doesn’t like our people, but it is not true. “I know what he has done here, I know what he has done in the North-West, and he has done extremely well,” he said. Bichi specifically mentioned Kano, Jigawa, Katsina, Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara among the states that had benefited from the President’s development initiatives. He expressed confidence that the people of Kano would demonstrate their appreciation for the president’s contributions. He added that he would provide further details of the projects executed in the state. item.title: Ajaero recalls 30-year bond as NLC scribe Ugboaja goes home
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — President of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Comrade Joe Ajaero, has paid an emotional tribute to the late National Secretary of the Congress, Comrade Emmanuel Ugboaja, describing him as more than a brother and recalling their 30-year relationship built on friendship, shared struggles and comradeship. Ajaero spoke on Saturday at Ugboaja’s burial in his Nkpa community, Abia State, where he said the depth of their personal relationship made him feel he was not the right person to deliver a tribute to the deceased. “Ugboaja was not just a friend. I don’t know how else to describe him. He was more than a brother. We shared the same fate. We are brothers in Christ and comrades in this family. We shared secrets. I found in him part of me,” he said. Describing the deceased as a perfect gentleman and one of the finest personalities in the labour movement, Ajaero said Ugboaja was dependable, courageous and committed to the interests of ordinary Nigerians, despite his connections with influential people. According to him, the late labour leader maintained relationships with successive presidents and presidential committees without allowing such connections to compromise his solidarity with the masses. “He knows the high and the mighty, yet he tilts towards the masses. If you have the most difficult assignment, give it to him to deliver. He doesn’t mince words in calling a spade a spade,” Ajaero said. He recalled that Ugboaja remained committed to his responsibilities even during his prolonged illness, disclosing that he was still attending to pressing matters at the NLC office barely three days before his death. Ajaero expressed confidence that his departed friend had gone to rest in the bosom of the Lord. Speaking on behalf of the family, the deceased’s immediate younger brother, Patrick Ugboaja, described him as an exceptional individual whose life was defined by service, sacrifice and concern for humanity. He said the deceased was his role model and a dependable source of guidance, adding that following in his footsteps had not been easy. “I have always looked up to him for direction. He was one person who had an answer to almost everything. When this happened, I looked around and wondered what he would have advised me to do,” he said. Patrick said his brother fought for the rights of the oppressed and touched countless lives across communities and beyond Nigeria. He expressed gratitude to dignitaries, labour leaders, friends and sympathisers who travelled from different parts of the country to honour the late unionist. In his sermon, the officiating preacher urged Nigerians to live purposeful lives, stressing that death was inevitable irrespective of one’s position, wealth, academic qualifications or influence. He challenged political leaders, public office holders, professionals and ordinary citizens to build enduring legacies through justice, forgiveness, humility and service to humanity. item.title: 2027: Diri charges Bayelsa APC to deny opposition 25% votes
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa Governor Douye Diri of Bayelsa State has charged members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state to intensify grassroots mobilisation to ensure that no opposition party secures 25 per cent of the votes in the 2027 presidential and National Assembly elections. Diri gave the charge at the grand finale of the Bayelsa East Renewed Hope Movement sensitisation campaign in Ogbia Town, where he urged party members to consolidate their political gains and reach out to undecided voters ahead of the elections. Represented by his deputy, Dr Peter Akpe, the governor said the APC could not afford to become complacent despite its political standing in the state, insisting that members must sustain their mobilisation efforts to secure an overwhelming victory. He also commended political leaders and stakeholders in Bayelsa East for embracing reconciliation and sustaining peace, describing unity as essential to the political and developmental progress of the area. Speaking on behalf of the governor, Akpe said the party appreciated the sacrifices and commitment of its members, particularly those who attended the event despite the rain. He, however, warned that the mobilisation drive must continue, urging party leaders to bring undecided voters into the APC fold. “But saying thank you does not mean you should go to sleep. It is time to dot the i’s and cross the t’s. One or two people are out there waiting for us to harvest. Bring them inside. Do not leave them outside because we want to squeeze the opposition to zero point. “Our winning is sure, but if we score 75 per cent, we have not won because the other people should not get 25 per cent. I emphasise that no opposition party or candidate should get 25 per cent of votes in Bayelsa,” he said. In his remarks, the Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), Dr Samuel Ogbuku, claimed that former President Goodluck Jonathan had endorsed President Bola Tinubu and all APC candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Ogbuku said APC candidates from Bayelsa East had visited Jonathan to seek his permission and blessings before commencing their sensitisation campaign. He said the former president had endorsed the candidates and encouraged them to work towards victory in the forthcoming elections. “As a people who respect leadership, we first took all our candidates to see the former president of Nigeria, Dr Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, who is also from this electoral district, to seek his permission and his blessings. “In that meeting, the former president actually blessed this movement, blessed our candidates and endorsed all of them, from president to the least candidate, and gave us a mandate to go out to win the election for the senatorial district,” Ogbuku said. item.title: Atiku pledges Mambilla completion, end to unnecessary taxes if elected
item.description: BAUCHI — Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to complete the long-abandoned Mambilla Hydropower Project in Taraba State if elected president in the 2027 general election. Atiku also promised to restore petrol subsidy, reintroduce electricity subsidy and abolish what he described as unnecessary taxes imposed on Nigerians. He made the pledges on Saturday at the ADC presidential campaign rally in Bauchi, where he urged residents of the North-East to support his party in the forthcoming election. The former Vice-President said the North-East was endowed with enormous mineral resources, including crude oil, but successive administrations had failed to harness the region’s potential for the benefit of its people. “I promise you that, by God’s grace, if you vote for us, we will ensure this oil work is completed for the prosperity of the North-East,” he said in Hausa. Speaking on the Mambilla Hydropower Project, Atiku recalled that successive governments had made promises to execute the project without bringing it to completion. “For those of you who are older, you will recall that since the era of Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, there have been promises to build a dam called the Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project, which past governments failed to actualise. “If God gives us the opportunity, and ADC is voted into power along with me, I promise you that we will continue and complete that project,” he said. On taxation, the ADC candidate pledged that his administration would eliminate taxes he considered unnecessary and unjustified. He also promised to tackle insecurity and banditry in the North-East, warning that those responsible for criminal activities would not be allowed to operate with impunity under his administration. “Finally, we know that here in the North-East, we face insecurity issues and banditry. I swear, if the president were not somehow, nobody would dare to commit this nonsense under my watch and get away with it,” he said. Atiku urged residents to vote for the ADC in 2027 and protect their votes until they were officially recorded. The former Vice-President also thanked Bauchi State Governor, Bala Mohammed, for providing the party access to the stadium and government lodges for its campaign rally, despite the ADC being in the opposition. “The Bauchi State governor did not take things too far, he gave us the opportunity to campaign in this stadium and provided us with all the government lodges. For doing that, we thank him, even though we remain in the opposition,” he said. Mambilla project and contractual dispute The Mambilla Hydropower Project, located in Taraba State, was conceived in 1972 under the military administration of former Head of State, General Yakubu Gowon, but has remained uncompleted for decades. item.title: US Thrash Haiti As Pochettino Prepares For Farewell
item.description: The United States thrashed Haiti 6-0 to surge towards the CONCACAF Nations League semi-finals on Saturday as Mauricio Pochettino’s penultimate game in charge ended in an emphatic victory. Goals from Christian Pulisic (2), Auston Trusty, Julian Hall, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun gave the US a commanding first-leg advantage to all but settle the outcome of the quarter-final before Tuesday’s second leg in Cincinnati. The build-up to Saturday’s fixture in Miami had been overshadowed by news of Pochettino’s departure as US coach after agreeing to take over Manchester United. But there was little sign that news of Pochettino’s exit had disturbed US preparations as they demolished World Cup qualifiers Haiti to deliver the biggest victory of the Argentine coach’s two-year reign. “Pochettino is an amazing manager, and he’s added a lot to us with the national team,” goalscorer Balogun said afterwards. “It’s always sad when you see a top coach leave, but it’s a part of the sport. “I think it was just important for us today to stick together and get the win — it just makes the send-off better,” Balogun added. Trusty gave the Americans the lead after just 10 minutes, confidently finishing from close range after Sebastian Berhalter’s free-kick from the right flank. Fans of Haiti cheer during the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match between Haiti and United States at Nu Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami, Florida. JC Ruiz/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by JC Ruiz / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) That goal was all that separated the teams at half-time, but the floodgates opened after the break. Hall calmly tucked away Antonee Robinson’s low cross in the 52nd minute after a sweeping counter-attack to make it 2-0. Pulisic made it 3-0 from the penalty spot 10 minutes later after being brought down in the box by Haiti defender Carlens Arcus. The AC Milan forward then grabbed his second goal a minute later, rifling into the bottom corner from the edge of the area to make it 4-0. McKennie’s 68th-minute header put Pochettino’s side 5-0 up, and the US thought they had added a sixth soon afterwards when Balogun shrugged off Arcus to score from close range. Weston McKennie #8 of United States celebrates scoring his team’s fifth goal during the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match between Haiti and United States at Nu Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami.(Photo by JC Ruiz / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) A VAR review, however, determined that Balogun had fouled Arcus in the build-up and the goal was chalked off. Balogun did not have long to wait, though, for his 13th international goal, latching on to a Malik Tillman through ball to score in the 82nd minute. item.title: CHINA DIARIES: The Future of farming
item.description: When we talk about China’s development, the images that often come to mind are high-speed trains, towering skyscrapers, electric vehicles and impressive infrastructure. But there is another quiet revolution taking place, one that is just as important to China’s future: agriculture. I had an opportunity to explore this during a visit to Yangling, in Shaanxi Province, a place that has become an important centre for agricultural science, research, innovation and technology. Our visit took us to three facilities: the SCO Demonstration Base for Agricultural Technology Exchange and Training, the Yangling Smart Agriculture Demonstration Park, and Yangling Liangke Agricultural Science and Technology Co. Ltd. What I saw offered an interesting glimpse into how China is using science and technology to rethink farming, improve productivity and strengthen food security. China Diaries: An Emperor, 8,000 Soldiers and a Lesson for Nigeria! 2027: We’ll fight Tinubu in South, North-Central, sweep North-West, North-East – Amaechi And, naturally, it got me thinking about Nigeria. Where farming meets the digital age One of the most interesting parts of the visit was seeing how technology is being integrated into everyday agricultural activities. At the smart agriculture demonstration facility, I saw a control station where plants are monitored through screens. Rather than relying entirely on physical observation, information about growing conditions can be monitored centrally, allowing operators to keep track of what is happening inside the growing facilities. It was a reminder that modern farming is increasingly becoming a data-driven activity. The farmer of the future may still walk through the farm, inspect the crops and get his hands dirty, but technology is giving him additional tools to make better decisions. I also saw vegetables being cultivated indoors in a controlled environment. It was fascinating to see food production taking place in a setting that looked quite different from the conventional farms we are familiar with in Nigeria. The idea is to manage growing conditions and create a more controlled environment for production. Such systems can help reduce dependence on some external weather conditions and make production more predictable, although their commercial viability depends on energy, infrastructure and operating costs. Another interesting sight was the display of grains and seedlings. These may look ordinary at first glance, but they represent an important part of the agricultural value chain: research, seed development and the effort to improve the quality and productivity of crops before they even get to the farm. Then came the agricultural drones. I photographed drones designed to spray farmland. Their use illustrates how technology can help farmers cover large areas more efficiently and apply agricultural treatments with greater precision.
